_why: `--allow-historical` exists to REPLACE mass-silencing: raising a document's provenance sha demotes every PINDRIFT at once without repairing a pin (measured on gateway-consolidation.design.md -- v1.15 FAIL issues=41, v1.16 PASS issues=0, 26 findings advisory, zero pins repaired). Under `in` the replacement reintroduced the disease at smaller scale: declaring `foo.py:1` also silenced `foo.py:12`, `foo.py:150` and every other `foo.py:1*`. The shipped test could not see it -- `_TWO_PINS` uses two DIFFERENT files, so no same-file interaction was ever exercised. Both mutations below leave a run that still prints a verdict-shaped PRECHECK line, and both directions are attacked: matching too WIDELY silences undeclared pins, matching too NARROWLY silently stops demoting anything and every caller's declarations are ignored with no error.

mutations.name: a-declared-pin-silences-every-pin-it-is-a-prefix-of
mutations._mechanism: The original defect, restored. `in` matches anywhere in the span, and the span ENDS with the pin -- so `…py:1` is a substring of `…py:12`. One declaration takes out a whole family of undeclared pins and the verdict flips FAIL issues=2 -> PASS issues=0, which is exactly the provenance-raising this flag was added to replace.
mutations.replace: return any(a in span for a in allow_historical)

mutations.name: the-anchor-tightens-to-equality-and-demotes-nothing
mutations._mechanism: The over-correction, and the reason the fix is not `==`. The caller builds a repo-relative span (`h-mad/scripts/h_mad_precheck_doc.py:1`) while the documented and tested input is a BARE filename (`h_mad_precheck_doc.py:1`). Under equality nothing matches, every declaration is ignored, and there is no error to say so -- the operator sees their pin still reported as a finding and concludes the flag is broken rather than that they spelled it short.
mutations.replace: return any(span == a for a in allow_historical)

mutations.name: the-path-boundary-is-dropped
mutations._mechanism: Without the leading `/`, a bare suffix match returns. The token `foo.py:1` then matches `…/bar_foo.py:1` -- a DIFFERENT file whose name merely ends the same way. Narrower than the `in` defect and invisible to a test that uses only one filename stem, which is why it is scored separately rather than folded into mutation 1.
mutations.find: if target == a or target.endswith("/" + a):

mutations.name: a-leading-slash-token-is-silently-ignored
mutations._mechanism: Drop the `lstrip`. A token written `/foo.py:1` matched under the old `in` and silently stops matching once anchored, because a span cannot end with `//foo.py:1`. Nothing errors: the operator's declaration is discarded, the pin is still reported as a finding, and the flag reads as broken. A declaration ignored WITHOUT an error is worse than one refused.
